title: Retain bounded writer expansion and final sync scheduling experiments
question: Can bounded concurrent writers, smaller catalogs and scheduled final syncs improve complete jobs larger than the engine working allocation?
summary: Retain opt-in bounded writer paths and resource tradeoffs. The 8 GiB ceiling extension improves median elapsed 36.9%, and Linux batching improves the 8,192-file cell 49.6% with all required sync calls.

workloads: 2 GiB Linux high-fanout publication, codec, Partition and stratified exact cells, plus an 8 GiB writer-ceiling extension and wide UTF-16 header control.
2 GiB native Windows ordered Partition and stratified exact assignment transfer.

validation.summary: Full native output and membership oracles on each timed job. Native format, lint and workspace checks plus Chromium bounded functional and resource checks. Default production build artifacts restored.

limitations: Linux WSL2 runs use a 1 GiB cgroup with no swap and uncontrolled backing caches. Windows uses NTFS with no OS memory cap.
Higher writer capacity trades working memory and file handles for less staging. Sync scheduling is Linux-only.
Comparators have different publication contracts. Three pairs do not establish tail latency. Raw originals remain local.
exclusions: Warmups, rejected prototypes, Windows harness failures and the interrupted Linux pair with no complete outer clock.
reopen_when: Test candidate selectors and workload transfer with new identified cells before a default activation decision.
